newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Philippine peso ends steady in range trading.
newsitem.headline: Philippine peso ends steady in range trading.

text.p: * Forex steady despite foreign equities selling
The Philippine peso closed unchanged at the day's low of 26.269 on Tuesday in narrow range trading, dealers said.
"Banks were buying dollars because some foreign funds were pulling out of the equities market," said a local bank trader.
Traders said the peso could have weakened but the Central Bank said it was willing to sell dollars at 26.27. "It (the bank) just stood at 26.27," a dealer said.
The day's average was at 26.268 from 26.266. Market volume rose to $96.50 million from $84.0 million.
Another dealer believed that some banks may have been buying dollars speculatively. "They're positioning on long dollars," he said.

He added banks are still betting the Central Bank would bring down its overnight rates following Friday's news of a 4.4 percent September inflation compared to August's 7.9. This would make the peso less attractive to hold versus the dollar.
The Central Bank has kept its overnight lending and borrowing rate at 13.0 and 11.0 percent respectively.
